entries.title: Hebrews 7:1
segments: Melchizedek. The name means King of righteousness.  A mysterious person appearing but once in the Old Testament (

), here introduced as a priest of a higher order than that of Aaron.  His priesthood was typical
 
of the eternal priesthood of Christ.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:3
segments: Without father, without mother. The priestly office of the sons of Aaron and the Levites was theirs by inheritance, not by any inherent holiness of life.  But Melchizedek had no priestly pedigree, and in this respect resembled Christ.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:16
segments:
Carnal commandment. Not according to the law of natural or physical descent, as in the Aaronic priesthood.
 

 
 Power of an endless life. A sentence implying that the priesthood of Jesus is his by virtue of his being the Son of God who liveth forever.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:18
segments: A disannulling of a foregoing commandment. The old testament was a stepping stone from discipline to something new and better.  The Mosaic code could not but fail to bring men into complete reconciliation with God.  This could only be done by spiritual contact with God through faith in Jesus Christ.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:19
segments: Better hope. Historical manifestation of Christ as spiritual Saviour of mankind.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:24
segments: Unchangeable. He ever liveth to intercede for us.  Our love and service vary; he abideth faithful.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:25
segments: The uttermost. From the lowest depths to the greatest heights; salvation from the guilt and power of sin.  See

entries.title: Hebrews 7:26
segments:
Became us. The Son of God met and answered the needs of those to whom he came.
 

 
 Holy. Entirely consecrated and set apart in voluntary obedience to the will of God.
 

 
 Guileless. Harmless without deceit.
 

 
 Undefiled. Pure and clean as touching the requirements of the ceremonial law.

entries.title: Hebrews 7:28
segments: Perfected.  Christ met every test and fulfilled every requirement the law could demand.  By his life, his suffering, his death, and his resurrection he became the perfect reconciler of mankind to God, and the perfect Saviour.
